About the tune

  • Music (Christian Lyre, 1831): Joshua Leavitt (fl. 1831)

Metre: 8.7.8.7. Hymns on this site in the same metre: Jesus, Tender Shepherd, Hear Me.

Melody from the Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (CCEH, public domain); tune PLEADING SAVIOR by Joshua Leavitt (fl. 1831). The CCEH gives its tunes as four-part scores; this page has the melody only, read from its MIDI file and checked against its incipit, and NoteFusion's engine wrote the solfa from the notes. It has not yet been checked against a printed hymn book.

Questions about Pleading Savior

What is the doh of Pleading Savior?

In this version, in F major, doh is F. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does Pleading Savior start on?

It starts on m (A in F major). Find doh first, then sing up or down to m.

What words can be sung to Pleading Savior?

Pleading Savior is in the metre 8.7.8.7: lines of 8, 7, 8, 7 syllables. Words written in the same metre fit it, such as Jesus, Tender Shepherd, Hear Me; check where the stresses fall before you sing them together.

Is Pleading Savior in the public domain?

Yes. Joshua Leavitt's work dates from 1831; the tune was first published in 1831. Everyone named died before 1955 and it was published before 1929, so the tune is out of copyright in Nigeria, the UK, the EU and the United States. Modern arrangements of it can still be under copyright.
